newsitem.title: FRANCE: French PM sees long haul to end Corsica violence.
newsitem.headline: French PM sees long haul to end Corsica violence.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, unfazed by Corsican separatist threats, pledged on Tuesday to crack down on the guerrillas' activities but conceded Paris faced a long haul to end bombings on the Mediterranean island.
Two new bombs exploded overnight in the southern Corsican town of Bonifacio and a third was defused in Porto Vecchio. No one was hurt in the blasts.

"I will not let myself be intimidated neither by threats, be they personal, nor by lies," Juppe told the National Assembly in Paris, renewing denials of charges by a separatist leader that the government secretly held abortive peace talks with nationalists earlier this year.

Juppe, 51, who is also mayor of Bordeaux, has adopted an increasingly tough line against the guerrillas since his offices at city hall in the southwestern city, were damaged in a nighttime bombing last month.
He said on Tuesday he would stick to a twin policy of clamping down on separatists while promoting economic, social and cultural development on the island.
"This policy will take time to succeed, and we will take it," he added. "It will require courage and I know that you and I have that."

Battling criticism that the crackdown has proved toothless, Justice Minister Jacques Toubon said 26 people had been rounded up in recent months on suspicion of offences linked to the guerrilla violence.
"Judicial procedures are continuing against them, and against people yet to be identified or detained," he said.
One of the bombs overnight in Bonifacio wrecked the parked car of the town's mayor and the other damaged the door to a local restaurant. No one immediately claimed responsibility.
The defused bomb was outside the office of the mayor's wife -- a doctor -- in Porto Vecchio.

The attacks came 24 hours after the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), "Historic Wing", the island's most hardline separatist group, claimed responsibility for a blast at the home of Emile Zuccarelli, a former cabinet minister and currently mayor of the northern Corsican town of Bastia. He was not at home and no one was hurt.
In a statement to the media, the FLNC had also claimed responsibility for 17 other attacks since early September, including the bombing of law courts, postal offices and banks.
